reference.title: Help JSON API reference
reference.shortdesc: For apps that render help in their own UI: the same filtered help as the panel, as JSON.

section.title: Authentication and CORS
section.p: Send an embed token, the same kind the widget uses, on every request: Authorization: Bearer <token>. See .

ul.li: Browser requests must come from one of the allowed embed origins; others get 403 {"error":"origin not allowed"}. Requests without an Origin header, such as from your backend, are allowed.
Preflight OPTIONS requests are answered for allowed origins, permitting GET and the authorization header.
Responses are sent with Cache-Control: private, no-store.

section.title: GET /api/v1/help/context
section.p: The help for a context. Query parameters: app (required), and key or path. Resolves as described in .
section.codeblock: { "key": "tenants", "via": "parent", "fragment": null, "topicId": "topics/next/console", "title": "Operator console (coming soon)", "shortdesc": "…", "html": "<article class=\"concept topic\" id=\"console\">…</article>", "related": [], "fullUrl": "https://docs.example.com/topics/next/console.html", "embedUrl": "https://docs.example.com/embed/topics/topics/next/console.html" }

property.propdesc: The key that matched, and how: key, parent or default.
The element or nested topic to scroll to, or null. It is null when that element is filtered out for this reader, so it never names a section they cannot see.
Plain text, filtered for the reader.
The topic as an HTML article, filtered for the reader, with absolute links to the docs site. Sanitize or sandbox it like any HTML you did not write.
Up to eight visible children and siblings in the navigation.
The page on the docs site, and in the panel.

section.title: GET /api/v1/help/topics/<topicId>
section.p: One topic by page id, such as /api/v1/help/topics/topics/help/widget. Same fields as above, without key, via and fragment.

section.title: GET /api/v1/help/nav
section.p: The reader's table of contents, for a help sidebar: filtered exactly as the docs site's contents. Topics the reader cannot see are left out, and never lend their title to anything; a heading with nothing visible under it is left out too, and so are toc="no" entries.

property.propdesc: The site's title, and the release and release line the reader is served.
The entries, in map order. Each has a title and children; a topic also has its topicId, which /api/v1/help/topics/ accepts. An entry without topicId is a heading, and always has children.

section.title: GET /api/v1/help/search?q=
section.p: Searches only the topics this reader can see, and only the parts of them this reader can see. Every word must appear, in any form (installing finds install). Quote a phrase ("setup wizard"), use or between alternatives, and put - before a word to exclude it. The last word also matches as a prefix, for search as you type. Title matches weigh most, then the short description, then the body. Up to ten hits, best first; score is a relative rank.

strow.stentry: The token is missing, invalid or expired.
The origin is not allowed, the email is not a registered reader of that organization, or the organization has no entitlements.
No help for this context, no such topic (or one the reader cannot see), or nothing published yet for the reader's release line.

section.title: Images
section.p: Image URLs in html point at the docs site and need a docs session. If your app renders help natively and the topics contain gated images, proxy them through your backend.
